about: Tags offered as concept pages and declined by the writer (pipeline/lib/concepts.mjs). A declined tag is offered again once CONCEPTS.reofferFactor times as many briefings carry it. Delete an entry to have the tag offered at the next run.

admin-center.reason: Admin centre names a family of portals (Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Apps, Viva Engage) where settings live, not one mechanism with its own behaviour, cost or controls. The briefings depend on unrelated settings in different portals, so each belongs on its own mechanism's page.

admin-controls.reason: Admin controls is a broad category that spans many admin centres, products and settings, not one mechanism with its own behaviour, licence or cost. The controls are documented per feature, and each briefing's own controls table already lists them.

adoption.reason: Adoption is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings carrying it cover unrelated features (Edge start-up, PowerPoint Presenter View, Teams notifications, Viva Insights reporting) with no shared behaviour, controls or cost to explain.

agent-governance.reason: Agent governance is a broad category, not one mechanism. Its briefings rest on separate mechanisms that have their own pages (work-iq, mcp, data-policies, agent-identity, managed-environments), and the Agent 365 registry is a product surface, not a distinct mechanism.

ai.reason: "AI" is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings span unrelated products (Teams, Power Apps, Purview, Dynamics 365) with different controls and costs. The shared AI billing meter is already explained by the copilot-credits concept page.

analytics.reason: Analytics is a broad category, not one mechanism. The briefings tagged with it cover unrelated products with separate controls and costs, such as Viva Insights, Agent 365 Business Analytics, Power Automate process mining, Teams call and meeting reports, and Dynamics 365.

authentication.reason: Authentication is a broad category, not one mechanism. The briefings span Entra passkeys, Conditional Access contexts, Power Pages identity providers, OAuth for connectors and credential vaults, which share no behaviour, controls or cost. Agent sign-in is already explained by the agent-identity page.

automation.reason: Automation is a broad category, not one mechanism: its briefings span Power Automate desktop flows, Copilot Studio workflows, Teams Workflows, agent lifecycle rules and a OneDrive command-line tool, each with its own licence and controls.

channels.reason: The tag mixes two senses: Teams channels, a workspace area of one product that eight briefings touch in unrelated ways (backup, notifications, apps, workflows), and the surfaces a Copilot Studio agent is published to, which only one briefing depends on. Neither is one mechanism with its own cost and controls.

copilot-control-system.reason: Copilot Control System is Microsoft's umbrella name for a collection of admin controls, reports and policies across several products, not one mechanism with its own behaviour or cost. The mechanisms inside it, such as Copilot Credits and spending policies, have or suit their own concept pages.

cost-management.reason: Cost management is a broad category, not one mechanism. Its Copilot spending policies, Cost Management configuration and consumption views are already explained by the copilot-credits page; the storage meters and flow groups are separate features.

data-export.reason: Data export is a label for unrelated features with different controls, licences and destinations (scanner SQL reports, Viva metric downloads, eDiscovery packages, CSV downloads, Application Insights and Fabric). No single mechanism ties them together.

data-governance.reason: Data governance is a broad category, not one mechanism: its briefings span DLP, auto-labelling, audit, eDiscovery, Organizational Data Service and SharePoint reports, and existing pages such as data-policies, sensitivity-labels, endpoint-dlp, auditing and ediscovery already explain the mechanisms.

data-lifecycle-management.reason: Data lifecycle management is the name of a Microsoft Purview solution area, not one mechanism: its briefings cover retention, Priority cleanup, archive mailboxes, PST import and bulk delete. Retention, its core mechanism, is already explained by the existing concept page `retention`.

delegation.reason: The tag labels unrelated features: Teams call delegates, Viva leader delegates, administrative-unit scoping of admin roles, delegated prompt publishing and Power Apps query delegation. Each has its own controls and cost, so there is no single mechanism to explain.

extensibility.reason: Extensibility is a broad category, not one mechanism: its briefings span custom engine agents, MCP servers, Copilot connectors, the Dataverse Python SDK and Power Pages client APIs, each with different controls. The shared parts are already explained on the mcp and connectors concept pages.

finops.reason: FinOps names a practice, not one mechanism: the briefings span Copilot Credits, Process licence capacity, pay-as-you-go storage meters and savings rules, each with its own controls. Copilot Credits and spending policies are already explained on /concepts/copilot-credits/ and /concepts/spending-policies/.

governance.reason: Governance is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings under it cover unrelated controls (Teams app availability, data policies, Purview roles, site lifecycle policies). Existing pages such as data-policies, managed-environments and security-roles already explain the specific mechanisms.

human-in-the-loop.reason: Human in the loop is a design pattern, not one mechanism. The briefings that carry it cover unrelated settings in Business Central, Customer Service, Viva Engage, Copilot Studio and Work IQ, each with its own controls, roles and cost, so there is no shared behaviour or control surface to explain once.

information-protection.reason: Information protection is a broad Purview solution area, not one mechanism: its briefings span auto-labeling, DLP conditions, sensitive information types and label inheritance. Labels and encryption are already explained by the sensitivity-labels concept page.

licensing.reason: Licensing is a broad category spanning Microsoft 365 Copilot, Power Platform, Planner and Viva, each with its own licences and rules, not one mechanism. Usage metering is already explained by the copilot-credits and spending-policies concept pages, and Managed Environments covers its own licensing condition.

m365-admin-center.reason: The Microsoft 365 admin centre is an admin portal, a place where many mechanisms (agent registry, backup, billing, Copilot settings) live, not one mechanism with its own behaviour, cost or controls. Those mechanisms are better explained on pages of their own.

migration.reason: Migration is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings cover unrelated moves (Google Workspace tools, Lifecycle Services to Power Platform admin center, PST import, EWS to Graph, a Teams device portal) with different controls, costs and licensing.

mobile.reason: Mobile is an app type, the iOS and Android clients, not one mechanism. The briefings that carry it depend on unrelated controls (Teams policies, Intune app protection, Purview labels and DLP), each explained on its own page.

model-driven-apps.reason: Model-driven apps are an app type, a place where mechanisms live, not one mechanism with its own cost and controls. The briefings depend on separate settings (form fill assistance, row summaries, display density, Work IQ access) that each belong on their own page.

monitoring.reason: Monitoring is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings span Purview alerts, Copilot Studio cost views, Teams troubleshooting, Application Insights and Edge alerts, each with its own controls and cost. Audit logging is already explained by the auditing concept page.

oversharing.reason: Oversharing names a risk that spans several separate mechanisms (site discovery limits, sensitivity labels, DLP, data access governance reports, maker credentials), not one mechanism with its own behaviour. Existing concept pages already explain the main controls.

policy.reason: Policy is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings span unrelated policy types (Edge Group Policy settings, Teams calling and messaging policies, Purview DLP policies, Work IQ MCP policy), each with its own controls, licensing and admin centre.

power-platform-admin-center.reason: The Power Platform admin centre is an admin portal, a place where many separate mechanisms live, not one mechanism. Its controls are better explained by concepts such as Managed Environments, Copilot Credits and data policies.

powershell.reason: PowerShell is an administration surface shared by many separate modules (Teams, Exchange, SharePoint, Viva), not one mechanism with its own behaviour, cost or controls. Each cmdlet belongs to the briefing and product whose setting it changes.

privacy.reason: Privacy is a broad category, not one mechanism. The briefings tagged with it cover unrelated controls (Teams recording templates, Edge tracking prevention, Purview audit events, Copilot sharing), each with its own settings, licensing and behaviour.

sharing.reason: Sharing is a broad category, not one mechanism: the briefings span agent sharing in Copilot Studio, SharePoint and OneDrive links, Teams screen sharing, Outlook folders and Copilot responses, each with separate controls. Agent sharing limits are already explained by the managed-environments page.

threat-detection.reason: Threat detection is a broad category, not one mechanism. The briefings under it are separate features with different controls and licensing (Teams phishing and QR code checks, external bot handling, deepfake detection, Copilot Studio credential sharing), so each is better served by its own briefing.

user-experience.reason: User experience is a broad category describing any change to how a feature looks or behaves, not one mechanism with its own controls or cost. The 64 briefings span unrelated products (Teams, Edge, Access, Copilot, Planner), each with different controls.

write-actions.reason: Write actions is a kind of behaviour shared by unrelated products (OneNote, Planner, Work IQ, federated connectors), not one mechanism with its own controls or cost. Each depends on its own controls, covered by the existing work-iq, mcp and connectors concept pages.
